Its position is contested less by a named firm than by the alternatives its customers already have: customers can substitute substitute materials at the customer's plant and automation absorbing the task itself, and the economics that decide the contest are high operating leverage — cost per unit is largely fixed against a price that is not, so margin swings by more than price does. Internal intelligence — what is still bounded These are the measures a business of this kind is judged on that the public record did not supply. Each one is a magnitude the analysis above had to leave in direction only. produced volume — the half of revenue the company controls. realised price versus benchmark — the other half, which it does not. unit cash cost — position on the industry cost curve. reserve life or resource base — how long the volume lasts. sustaining capital — what it costs to keep volume flat. On the roadmap CRM and pipeline Which deals moved, which stalled, and why. This is what separates a pricing hypothesis from a pricing answer. On the roadmap Customer feedback What buyers say when they are not filling in a renewal form. On the roadmap Decision log What leadership considered, chose, and rejected — with the reasons, so the next decision starts from the last one. What a private company intelligence keeps A recommendation is not a decision, and a decision is not an act. The system keeps them separate and remembers each one as its own kind of thing. Recommendation What the analysis put forward, and the evidence standing behind it at the time. Human decision What leadership actually chose — including choosing not to act, which is a decision and is usually recorded nowhere. Action What was then done, by whom, and when.
